lean.annotation: Write $T_j$ for the $T$-gate bound at time $t=j+1$ and $Q$ for the common logical width. The formula in `stoppingPower_const_cost` counts $50Q\sum_jT_j$ for all 500 evolutions. Dividing by 500 yields the arithmetic mean $Q\sum_jT_j/10$ for the ten times.

lean.name: QuantumComputation.Specs.stoppingPowerProgram
lean.plain: Circuit for evolution to t = j + 1
lean.annotation: The index $j$ picks both the number of segments and how each segment is constructed. For example, the Hamiltonian error cap for the block encoding decreases from $0.009762677$ Ha at $t=1$ to $0.000892$ Ha at $t=10$. The 50 runs at any one time all use the same circuit.

lean.name: QuantumComputation.Specs.stoppingPower_const_cost
lean.annotation: The second conjunct sums the ten circuits’ $T$-gate bounds, taking the larger count at each conditional. It multiplies this sum by 50 for the repeated evolutions and by the common logical width to bound the spacetime volume.

lean.annotation: `stoppingPowerProgram` constructs just the evolution circuit at one index $j$. For example, $j=4$ gives the circuit for $t=5$ a.u., which the sampling protocol runs 50 times on fresh inputs.

statements.markdown: the protocol repeats time evolution $50$ times at each of $t=1,\dots,10$ a.u. ($500$ runs)
to estimate the mean projectile kinetic energy, omitting state preparation and readout as their cost is negligible.
statements.note: The measured observable is the projectile kinetic energy $\|k_p-k_{\mathrm{proj}}\|_2^2/(2M_{\mathrm{proj}})$, which is diagonal in the projectile momentum basis. The 50 measurements give one mean at each time, and fitting the ten means gives an estimate of the rate of energy loss. State preparation, readout and the error of the fit are outside the evolution theorem.
